message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is a **placental mammal** that lived tens of millions of years ago.  
- Lions belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae).  
- Zebras belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  

These two orders diverged from a common ancestor that was part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which includes many modern mammalian groups such as carnivores, ungulates, bats, and whales. The most recent common ancestor of lions and zebras would have been a small, likely insect‑eating mammal that lived during the late Paleocene or early Eocene (about 55–60 million years ago). This ancestor would have possessed the basic mammalian body plan and would have given rise to the lineages that eventually led to the diverse carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates we see today.
